Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

## Diagnosis
The current bug report mentions changes made in a revision that triggered several issues in the optimization package of the system. Specifically, it mentions issues such as [MATH-394](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/MATH-394), [MATH-397](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/MATH-397), and [MATH-404](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/MATH-404). One of the issues collected in this report is related to the `BrentOptimizer` class, mentioning a specific convergence problem.

Looking at the failing test `testQuinticMin()`, the test sets up a `QuinticFunction`, a `BrentOptimizer` with specific parameters, and a `MultiStartUnivariateRealOptimizer`. It then calls `optimize` on the `optimizer` object with specific arguments and checks the result.

To investigate the failure further, we need to understand the implementation of the `BrentOptimizer` class and analyze how the recent changes in the revision may have impacted its convergence behavior.

## Code Analysis
